desc:
For every prefix nums[0..i] of the array, find its mode: the value that occurs most often in that prefix. If several values are tied for most occurrences, the mode is the smallest of them.

Return an array res where res[i] is the mode of the prefix ending at index i.

For example, [2, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3] gives [2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3].
hints: Recomputing the mode of every prefix from scratch costs O(n<sup>2</sup>). Update the counts incrementally instead.
Adding one element increases exactly one count by 1. So the maximum count either stays the same or grows by exactly 1, and only the touched value can become a new best.
Keep count, the current maximum count best and the current mode mode. After incrementing count[x]: if it exceeds best, then x is the sole leader; if it equals best, the mode becomes min(mode, x).
editorial: Only the value just added can change status. After count[x] increases: if count[x] > best, then x is now strictly ahead of everybody, so best = count[x] and mode = x. If count[x] == best, x has joined the tied group, and the smallest tied value is min(mode, x) because the old mode was already the smallest of the previous group. If it is below best nothing changes.

Every step is O(1) with a hash map, so the whole array takes O(n). The trick that makes the tie rule easy is that counts only ever grow: values never leave the leading group, so tracking its minimum is enough.
